key_terms.meaning: Sij = wave leaving port i divided by wave incident at port j, with every other port matched to its reference impedance.
The square matrix [S] that collects all Sij of an N-port; port voltages and currents are replaced by incident and reflected waves.
A waveguide tee whose branch arm lies in the plane of the electric field; when fed from the branch it gives a 180° phase relation between collinear outputs.
A waveguide tee whose branch arm lies in the plane of the magnetic field; it acts as a shunt split with in-phase collinear outputs when fed from the branch.
A four-port hybrid made from E-plane and H-plane tees; the collinear arms are matched, and the E arm and H arm are isolated from each other.
A four-port device; with input at port 1, port 3 samples forward power and port 4 receives little; C = 10 log10(P1/P3) dB and D = 10 log10(P3/P4) dB.
A closed-ring four-port, usually 3λg/2 long (λg is guide wavelength), that splits input equally into two outputs with 0° or 180° phase difference depending on port choice.
A passive network that divides input power among output ports in a designed ratio; a Wilkinson divider can match all ports and isolate outputs.
A two-port component that reduces power by a stated number of dB; attenuation A(dB) = 10 log10(Pin/Pout).
A two-port ferrite device that passes power in one direction with low loss and absorbs power in the reverse direction.
A multi-port ferrite device that sends power in a fixed cyclic order, such as port 1 to 2, 2 to 3, and 3 to 1.
A biased ferrite section changes the phase velocity of a microwave wave; changing the DC magnetic bias changes the phase shift.
A vacuum tube in which cavity velocity modulation bunches an electron beam; the bunched beam gives microwave amplification or oscillation.
A single-cavity klystron with a repeller electrode; the returning bunched beam sustains microwave oscillation.
A crossed-field vacuum tube with resonant cavities; the magnetic field makes electrons form a rotating spoke that drives cavity oscillations at high power.
A traveling-wave tube uses a helical slow-wave structure to keep an RF wave in step with an electron beam, giving broad-band microwave amplification.
A transferred-electron device showing negative differential resistance; biased above threshold it oscillates in a microwave cavity.
An avalanche transit-time diode; avalanche multiplication and transit delay create negative resistance for high-power microwave oscillation.
Voltage standing wave ratio = (1 + |Γ|)/(1 − |Γ|), where Γ is the reflection coefficient; it measures mismatch on a line.
A monolithic microwave integrated circuit puts passive and active microwave devices on one semiconductor substrate, with no discrete bond wires between them.

takeaways: S-parameters replace voltages and currents at microwave frequencies because waves at matched ports are easier to define and measure than open and short tests.
A tee's branch plane decides its E-plane or H-plane behaviour, and a magic tee combines both to give matched collinear arms with isolated E and H arms.
A directional coupler is specified by coupling, directivity and isolation, not only by the split ratio.
A hybrid ring gives an equal split with a fixed phase, so it can act as a 0° or 180° hybrid depending on the chosen ports.
Attenuation in dB adds directly; a 10 dB attenuator cuts power to one tenth.
Ferrite bias breaks reciprocity, enabling isolators, circulators and phase shifters.
Tubes remain useful where high power is needed; klystrons, magnetrons and TWTs use electron beams with cavities or slow-wave structures.
Gunn, IMPATT, TRAPATT and tunnel diodes generate microwave power by negative resistance without a heated cathode.
Microwave measurements use indirect methods: a slotted line for VSWR, power sensors for power, wavemeters for frequency, and a network analyser for S-parameters.
MIC and MMIC technology puts planar microwave circuits on a substrate, shrinking size and improving repeatability.

glossary.def: A terminal pair or waveguide opening where power enters or leaves a microwave network.
A load whose impedance equals the line reference impedance, so no wave reflects from it.
A ratio of an outgoing wave at one port to an incident wave at another port when all other ports are matched.
A network whose scattering matrix is symmetric, Sij = Sji, when all ports use the same impedance.
A network with no resistive loss; its scattering matrix is unitary, [S]†[S] = [I].
A waveguide tee with the branch arm in the plane of the electric field.
A waveguide tee with the branch arm in the plane of the magnetic field.
A four-port hybrid made from E-plane and H-plane tees, with matched collinear arms and isolated E and H arms.
A four-port passive device that couples a known fraction of forward power to a coupled port while giving low power to an isolated port.
Coupling C = 10 log10(P1/P3) dB, with input at port 1 and coupled port 3.
Directivity D = 10 log10(P3/P4) dB, the ratio of coupled-port power to isolated-port power.
Isolation I = 10 log10(P1/P4) dB, the ratio of input power to power at the isolated port; I = C + D.
A ring-shaped four-port hybrid that gives equal power split with a fixed 0° or 180° phase difference between outputs.
A passive network that divides input power between two or more outputs, often with matching and isolation.
A two-port device that reduces microwave power by a specified number of decibels.
A ferrite two-port that transmits in one direction and absorbs power in the reverse direction.
A ferrite multi-port that routes power in a fixed cyclic order, such as 1 to 2, 2 to 3, 3 to 1.
A magnetic ceramic material whose permeability becomes nonreciprocal under a DC magnetic bias.
A linear-beam vacuum tube that uses cavity velocity modulation and drift-space bunching to amplify microwaves.
A crossed-field vacuum tube with resonant cavities, used as a high-power microwave oscillator.
A wideband vacuum-tube amplifier in which a slow-wave helix keeps an RF wave in step with an electron beam.
A transferred-electron semiconductor device that shows negative resistance and oscillates when biased above a threshold field.
An avalanche transit-time diode that uses avalanche multiplication and transit delay to produce negative resistance at microwave frequencies.
Voltage standing wave ratio = (1 + |Γ|)/(1 − |Γ|), a measure of mismatch on a transmission line.
A calibrated instrument that measures amplitude and phase of S-parameters of a device over frequency.
A monolithic microwave integrated circuit in which passive and active devices are fabricated on one semiconductor chip.
